subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw own a custom cooperative glob implementation and an event-loop yield between bootstrap hook handlers in the core embedded-run path, rather than retain the native glob contract and address responsiveness at a narrower scheduling seam?
rationale: The patch is a plausible and well-evidenced performance repair, but it establishes lasting core compatibility and scheduling behavior that tests alone cannot calibrate against all existing configurations and hook consumers.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded core contract
options.body: Accept the cooperative walker and bootstrap-only hook yield after requiring final-head compatibility and live embedded-run proof.

options.title: Narrow the repair
options.body: Ask for a smaller owner-approved scheduling solution that avoids replacing native glob semantics in the bootstrap configuration path.

options.title: Pause the direction
options.body: Do not merge this branch if OpenClaw does not want to own a custom glob-parity implementation and hook scheduling contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Accept the cooperative walker and bootstrap-only hook yield after requiring final-head compatibility and live embedded-run proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining question is core runtime product direction; the timeline connects this person to the PR, though source-history attribution could not be completed from the supplied review material.
